original_value: The detection, quantification, diagnosis, and identification of plant diseases is particularly crucial for precision agriculture. Recently, traditional visual assessment technology has not been able to meet the needs of precision agricultural informatization development, and hyperspectral technology, as a typical type of non-invasive technology, has received increasing attention. On the basis of simply describing the types of pathogens and host–pathogen interaction processes, this review expounds the great advantages of hyperspectral technologies in plant disease detection. Then, in the process of describing the hyperspectral disease analysis steps, the articles, algorithms, and methods from disease detection to qualitative and quantitative evaluation are mainly summarizing. Additionally, according to the discussion of the current major problems in plant disease detection with hyperspectral technologies, we propose that different pathogens’ identification, biotic and abiotic stresses discrimination, plant disease early warning, and satellite-based hyperspectral technology are the primary challenges and pave the way for a targeted response.

result.paraphrase: Detecting, quantifying, diagnosing, and identifying plant diseases is especially important for precision agriculture. In recent years, traditional visual assessment methods have been unable to satisfy the demands of precision agricultural informatization, so hyperspectral technology, a representative non-invasive approach, has attracted growing attention. After briefly outlining pathogen types and host–pathogen interaction processes, this review highlights the significant advantages of hyperspectral techniques in plant disease detection. It then summarizes the articles, algorithms, and methods used in hyperspectral disease analysis, from detection through qualitative and quantitative evaluation. In addition, based on discussion of the main current problems in hyperspectral plant disease detection, it proposes that identification of different pathogens, discrimination between biotic and abiotic stresses, early warning of plant disease, and satellite-based hyperspectral technology are the key challenges and a basis for targeted responses.
